scope: The Saturday Spin site-side growth follow-through: focus /newsletter on one useful Saturday training letter; make podcast episode signup CTAs lead with The Saturday Spin and preserve podcast attribution; replace the Faster After 40 coaching squeeze with a report-to-newsletter acquisition path; and keep Faster After 40 free of global coaching conversion chrome. YouTube and Beehiiv editorial/automation operations remain outside this release.

sections.readerQuestion: What exactly will I receive if I subscribe to The Saturday Spin?
sections.usefulAnswer: One useful cycling training letter every Saturday: one clear takeaway, why it matters, and one practical action to use on the bike that week.
sections.evidence: Anthony supplied the active-list figure of about 23,215, rounded to 23,000 weekly readers. The exact PR merge rendered at 1440x1000 and 390x844 with the focused promise, 23,000-reader proof, no 30,000/65% claim and no horizontal overflow.
sections.editorialDecision: Remove podcast-digest and community-promo framing from the landing page. Keep the product promise narrow, useful and weekly while preserving the already-corrected 23,000 audience proof.

sections.location: Podcast episode EmailCapture — shared conversion path
sections.readerQuestion: What should a podcast listener be asked to do after consuming an episode, and can acquisition still be attributed to the episode?
sections.usefulAnswer: Podcast episode forms now lead with The Saturday Spin. They normalise acquisition source to podcast and retain the episode slug as the default UTM campaign, while explicit query UTM values can override that campaign.
sections.evidence: The shared EmailCapture implementation detects podcast and podcast-<slug> sources. The exact PR merge rendered both specified Stephen Seiler episode pages at desktop and mobile widths; each showed The Saturday Spin promise, returned HTTP 200 and had no horizontal overflow.
sections.editorialDecision: Use the newsletter as the primary listener conversion door without deleting the wider episode content or introducing a new Beehiiv list, automation or YouTube write.

sections.readerQuestion: What does a visitor get from Faster After 40, and what happens after they request it?
sections.usefulAnswer: The page offers the existing Faster After 40 report, then clearly states that the requester also joins The Saturday Spin. It describes the report in neutral terms around training, fuelling, strength and recovery and provides the existing on-site PDF download after a successful request.
sections.evidence: The old long-form coaching squeeze and its scoped CSS were removed. The exact PR merge rendered /faster-after-40 at 1440x1000 and 390x844 with HTTP 200, no horizontal overflow, the free-report CTA and Saturday Spin path, and none of the QA-forbidden sales strings including Not Done Yet, $195, 100M+, 113 riders, START APPLICATION or Community.
sections.editorialDecision: Treat Faster After 40 as a named-PDF acquisition surface rather than a coaching sales page. The PDF file itself is unchanged by this release and is not re-certified here.

sections.readerQuestion: Can Faster After 40 signups be attributed cleanly without creating a new Beehiiv workflow or risky custom field?
sections.usefulAnswer: The endpoint accepts named_pdf, podcast, youtube or site source values plus optional UTM source, medium and campaign. Attribution is passed through Beehiiv's native UTM fields; the existing last_lead_magnet custom field remains, and no new acquisition_source custom field is introduced.
sections.evidence: The existing Beehiiv helper maps source, medium and campaign to Beehiiv utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign. The exact merge build passed TypeScript and generated 4,466 static pages; no real subscriber was created during QA.
sections.editorialDecision: Use native Beehiiv UTM attribution and existing lead-magnet metadata only. Do not edit Beehiiv posts, automations, referral configuration or welcome automation.

sections.readerQuestion: Can the lead-magnet page remain a single-purpose acquisition experience without Roadman's global coaching overlays reappearing?
sections.usefulAnswer: Faster After 40 is now a lean route, so the global coaching conversion chrome does not load on that page.
sections.evidence: Earlier rendered QA identified $195 and START APPLICATION as global chrome rather than page content. Adding /faster-after-40 to the existing lean-route list removed those strings; the final exact-merge desktop and mobile browser checks found no forbidden sales strings.
sections.editorialDecision: Suppress only the global conversion chrome on this lead-magnet route. Leave Roadman's coaching conversion surfaces unchanged elsewhere.

claimsAndSources: The only audience number used in this release is Anthony's supplied Beehiiv active-list snapshot of about 23,215, rounded to 23,000. No open-rate claim, sponsor-performance metric, coaching member count, science efficacy claim or new Faster After 40 result claim is added. The existing Faster After 40 PDF body is unchanged.
examplesAndReasoning: A podcast episode form with source podcast-<episode-slug> resolves Beehiiv acquisition source to podcast and uses the episode slug as the default UTM campaign. Faster After 40 defaults to named_pdf, accepts approved source values plus optional UTM parameters, and sends attribution through Beehiiv's native UTM fields.
voiceAndCuts: The Saturday Spin copy was simplified around one useful training letter every Saturday. The Faster After 40 landing removes high-pressure coaching and community sales framing rather than replacing it with new performance hype. Podcast pages use the same plain Saturday Spin promise through the shared capture component.
desktopReview: Chromium rendered the exact PR merge revision at 1440x1000 for /newsletter, both specified Stephen Seiler podcast pages and /faster-after-40. All four returned HTTP 200, showed the intended newsletter/report messaging and had no horizontal overflow; the Faster After 40 route contained none of the forbidden coaching-sales strings.
mobileReview: Chromium rendered the exact PR merge revision at 390x844 for /newsletter, both specified Stephen Seiler podcast pages and /faster-after-40. All four returned HTTP 200, preserved the intended CTA/message hierarchy and had no horizontal overflow; Faster After 40 remained free of the forbidden coaching-sales strings.
productAndOfferAccuracy: This release does not edit YouTube, Beehiiv posts, Beehiiv automations, Beehiiv referral/reward configuration, Skool, Not Done Yet pricing or sponsor packages. The Faster After 40 PDF remains the existing report asset, and the Core Training Guide remains a separate referral reward rather than a newsletter signup incentive.
